startMenu._doc: ⚑ S219 / W1-B4 (walkthrough 1: 'the menu button doesn't do anything and it should… like the start menu, with all the stuff you can do, like the games, and it just tells you to go grab the handheld'). The taskbar's MENU opens LambyOS's own Start menu: NOW (the beat the piece is waiting on, with its hint), PROGRAMS (what is on this desktop, opened from here), IN THE ROOM (the era's ○ beats away from the screen: the handheld, the tapes, the racket…), Shut Down… (refused, S220) and Leave… (the frame's door, S220). Its words come from data/strings/map.json; only these labels are its own. The machine's voice: plain, period, never a quest log.

startMenu._docShut: ⚑ S220 (his, 2026-10-08: 'shut down should not work, but leave can… Shut down should pop up a message saying "you are not authorised to leave your treatment" or something'). Shut Down… is the machine's and the machine refuses (one line, OK, nothing filed); Leave… under it is the frame's door — it opens the game menu at the leave note (gameMenu.json leaveNote) and the plain page beyond it. The refusal is never the only way out.

witness._docEras: ⚑ S106 — THE RECORD AGES. One file, four decades, and until now every word on it was 1997's: the panel that migrates onto Maya's wall in 2026 still read SUBJECT Daniel / index · era 1 · drawer 12. The fields in `eras` are the ONLY ones that move, and they move because a filing system running for thirty years would have re-stamped exactly these — where the record came from, what it now calls the subject, and the stamp on the card. Everything else (the header, the dead FILE button, the footer's READ ONLY) is deliberately unchanged, because the point is that it did not have to change. ⚑ THE MISFILE, NOT A DEADNAME (CLAUDE.md; s4_l.json's _docFormerName): at era 4 the SUBJECT row carries Maya's OWN name and the amber note `under the old file`. No name that is not Maya's is ever rendered here. The index card underneath keeps the file's REGISTERED name — the one the player typed in 1997 — because that is what an index card in a drawer carries, and the gap between the two rows IS the beat: the system knows who she is and files her under someone else anyway. PLACEHOLDER-draft wording; Sérgio's stamp to overwrite (03_COORDINATION #5).

eras._note: keys are era ids; a missing key falls back to the flat era-1 wording above. ⚑ Eras 3 AND 4 are absent on purpose: the record is off the wall for 2016, and as of 2026-09-05 it is off for 2026 too — Sérgio retired the migration that used to carry it onto Maya's wall, so this panel now lives and ages entirely inside Daniel's own six years. dossier._doc: THE FOUND FILE (Session 60) — was 'Dossier — card 1 of 1', an authored card served front-and-centre on the desktop. Sérgio, 2026-07-26: 'Why is there a Dossier on the Desktop? Makes no sense'… then, answering it: 'it can stay as like an easter egg with a different name and like an explainer of the program.' So: KEPT, RENAMED, REPOSITIONED. Same family as S55's lamby_rig.exe, and inheriting its rules — never advertised, never rewarded (no toast), never drawn while any window is open (so it can never surface during a felt scene), filed silently. What died is the AUTHORING VOICE (the TACTIC/LAYER/STATUS/ARCHIVE furniture and the researcher note that leaked in S58) and the front-and-centre placement; what survives is the tactic content Sérgio called interesting, re-voiced as what it would actually be inside the fiction: the program's own orientation copy, explaining its referral route to its own people. ⚑ THE NAME AND EVERY LINE BELOW ARE SÉRGIO'S TO WRITE — this is in-world text and this is a PLACEHOLDER-draft for him to react to. The data key stays `dossier` so the ledger's own `dossier: ['card1']` entry and src/engine/app.ts's unlock call (both outside this session's file fence) keep working unchanged.
dossier._provenance: status: documentary — ex-gay-era referral routes (carried over unchanged from the card this file replaces; the enum lives here rather than on screen now that the window is diegetic). ⚑ ETHICS_CONSTRAINTS.md #13 says dossier cards carry a visible status — this file no longer renders one, because a STATUS line is the authoring voice Sérgio asked to have removed. Sérgio's call: keep provenance here (invisible, tracked), or restore a rendered line.
